Fig. 12 Digital image correlation (during bending) Fig. 13. The 3-point bending test results for As-cast and E-Coated alloys. Rectangular 3-point bend coupons 25 mm wide and 49 mm long were sheared from the 6HS2 and 6HS4 materials, where the length of the specimen was parallel with the rolling direction of the sheet. A portion 14 of the T4 specimens were artificially aged at 180°C +/- 2°C for 8 hours to a T6 temper using a Blue M electric convection air furnace. The 3-point bend testing was done using a VDA style knife punch with a tip radius of 0.4 mm and 30 mm diameter rollers spaced so that their center-to-center distance was 38 mm. A MTS SinTech screw driven load frame equipped with a 150 kN load cell was used to carry out 3- point bend testing. In this particular setup the punch was fixed at the base of the load frame while the rollers were mounted to a fixture that was connected to the loadcell enabling DIC measurement of the outer bend surface during the entirely of the 3-point bend test. The 3-point bend tests were run at a cross- head speed of 1 mm/s and terminated when load dropped 20% from the maximum test load. Strain of the outer bend surface was measured using an ARAMIS 3D 12M stereo camera digital image correlation (DIC) system using GOM Correlate Pro 2021 software. Two Schneider Xenoplane 50 mm f2.8 camera lens with 30.5 mm UV protectors were used, each lens was mounted to an ARAMIS 12M, 12 Megapixel sensor. The two sensor-lens assemblies were mounted on an adjustable bar so that the camera distance was 100 mm. The working measurement distance to the bend specimen was 314 mm. The angle between the two optical camera axes was 25°.
